arxiv-2103-11451.title: Holonomy of complex projective structures on surfaces with prescribed branch data
arxiv-2103-11451.creator: Thomas Le Fils
arxiv-2103-11451.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Thomas Le Fils. We characterize the representations of the fundamental group of a closed surface to PSL 2 ​ ( ℂ ) \mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{C}) that arise as the holonomy of a branched complex projective structure with fixed branch divisor. In particular, we compute the holonomies of the spherical metrics with prescribed integral conical angles and the holonomies of affine structures with fixed conical angles on closed surfaces.

arxiv-2105-04561.title: Long-time memory effects in a localizable central spin problem Journal: New J. Phys.
arxiv-2105-04561.creator: Eran Rabani
arxiv-2105-04561.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Eran Rabani. We study the properties of the Nakajima-Zwanzig memory kernel for a qubit immersed in a many-body localized (i.e. disordered and interacting) bath. We argue that the memory kernel decays as a power law in both the localized and ergodic regimes, and show how this can be leveraged to extract t → ∞ t\to\infty populations for the qubit from finite time ( J ​ t ≤ 10 2 Jt\leq 10^{2} ) data in the thermalizing phase.

arxiv-2110-09201.title: The formation of massive stellar clusters in converging galactic flows with photoionisation The formation of massive stellar clusters in converging galactic flows with photoionisation – References 2021
arxiv-2110-09201.creator: C. L. Dobbs, T. J. R. Bending, A. R. Pettitt, M. R. Bate
arxiv-2110-09201.description: Abstract We have performed simulations of cluster formation along two regions of a spiral arm taken from a global Milky Way simulation, including photoionising feedback. One region is characterised by strongly converging flows, the other represents a more typical spiral arm region.

arxiv-2112-08510.title: Conditions for realizing one-point interactions from a multi-layer structure model
arxiv-2112-08510.creator: Alexander V. Zolotaryuk and Yaroslav Zolotaryuk
arxiv-2112-08510.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexander V. Zolotaryuk and Yaroslav Zolotaryuk. A heterostructure composed of N N parallel homogeneous layers is studied in the limit as their widths l 1 , … , l N l_{1},\ldots,l_{N} shrink to zero. The problem is investigated in one dimension and the piecewise constant potential in the Schrödinger equation is given by the strengths V 1 , … , V N V_{1},\ldots,V_{N} as functions of l 1 , … , l N l_{1},\ldots,l_{N} , respectively.

arxiv-2305-05278.title: Crystal-Structure Matches in Solid-Solid Phase Transitions
arxiv-2305-05278.creator: Fang-Cheng Wang, Qi-Jun Ye, Yu-Cheng Zhu, Xin-Zheng Li
arxiv-2305-05278.description: Abstract The exploration of solid-solid phase transition suffers from the uncertainty of how atoms in two crystal structures match. We devised a theoretical framework to describe and classify crystal-structure matches (CSM). Such description fully exploits the translational and rotational symmetries and is independent of the choice of supercells.

arxiv-2512-10623.title: Generating wall-bounded turbulent inflows at high Reynolds numbers
arxiv-2512-10623.creator: Ronith Stanly 1, Timofey Mukha 2, Martin Karp 1, Stefano Markidis 3, Philipp Schlatter 1,4
arxiv-2512-10623.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ronith Stanly 1, Timofey Mukha 2, Martin Karp 1, Stefano Markidis 3, Philipp Schlatter 1,4. One of the main challenges in simulating high Reynolds number ( \Rey \Rey ) turbulent boundary layers (TBLs) is the long streamwise distance required for large-scale outer-layer structures to develop, making such simulations prohibitively expensive. We propose an inflow generation method for high \Rey \Rey wall turbulence that leverages the known structure and scaling laws of TBLs, enabling shorter development lengths by providing rich input information.

arxiv-2512-20642.title: Flow Gym
arxiv-2512-20642.creator: Francesco Banelli ETH Zürich fbanelli@ethz.ch, Antonio Terpin ETH Zürich aterpin@ethz.ch, Alan Bonomi ETH Zürich abonomi@ethz.ch, Raffaello D’Andrea ETH Zürich rdandrea@ethz.ch
arxiv-2512-20642.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francesco Banelli ETH Zürich fbanelli@ethz.ch, Antonio Terpin ETH Zürich aterpin@ethz.ch, Alan Bonomi ETH Zürich abonomi@ethz.ch, Raffaello D’Andrea ETH Zürich rdandrea@ethz.ch. Flow Gym is a toolkit for research and deployment of flow-field quantification methods inspired by OpenAI Gym [ 6 ] and Stable-Baselines3 [ 28 ] . It uses SynthPix [ 35 ] as synthetic image generation engine and provides a unified interface for the testing, deployment and training of (learning-based) algorithms for flow-field quantification from a number of consecutive images of tracer particles.

pmc-11380176.title: Does service-oriented manufacturing improve customer stability?
pmc-11380176.creator: Ling Ou
pmc-11380176.description: Stabilizing customer relationships plays an important role in improving supply chain resilience. Based on a sample of A-share listed companies in the manufacturing industry from 2009 to 2022, this work investigates the impact of SOM(service-oriented manufacturing) on supply chain resilience from the perspective of customer stability.

pmc-11397129.title: Dietary Carbohydrates, Genetic Susceptibility, and Gout Risk: A Prospective Cohort Study in the UK
pmc-11397129.creator: Baojie Hua, Ziwei Dong, Yudan Yang, Wei Liu, Shuhui Chen, Ying Chen, Xiaohui Sun, Ding Ye, Jiayu Li, Yingying Mao
pmc-11397129.description: This study aimed to investigate the associations between carbohydrate intake and gout risk, along with interactions between genetic susceptibility and carbohydrates, and the mediating roles of biomarkers. We included 187,387 participants who were free of gout at baseline and completed at least one dietary assessment in the UK Biobank.

pmc-11536265.title: Interaction between genetic risk score and dietary fat intake on lipid-related traits in Brazilian young adults
pmc-11536265.creator: Ramatu Wuni, Heyam Amerah, Serena Ammache, Nathália T Cruvinel, Nara R da Silva, Gunter G C Kuhnle, Maria A Horst, Karani S Vimaleswaran
pmc-11536265.description: The occurrence of dyslipidaemia, which is an established risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, has been attributed to multiple factors including genetic and environmental factors. We used a genetic risk score (GRS) to assess the interactions between genetic variants and dietary factors on lipid-related traits in a cross-sectional study of 190 Brazilians (mean age: 21 ± 2 years).

pmc-11558791.title: Sputum availability and quality in country-level TB prevalence surveys
pmc-11558791.creator: P. Papadopoulou, M. Gaeddert, A. Gupta-Wright, C.M. Denkinger, F.M. Marx
pmc-11558791.description: an adequate sputum sample is a known challenge, but its frequency among people accessing diagnostic services is not well established. Previous studies have shown that sputum scarcity is high in certain groups, such as people living with HIV (PLWH) and children.

pmc-12679240.title: HIF-1α modulates β-catenin pathway to enhance the survival and angiogenesis of PBMSCs under hypoxia environment
pmc-12679240.creator: Peng-Zhen Wang, Ai-Qun Wang, Ping-Ge Tian, Ping-Ping Zhu, Wei Yuan, Jian Wu, Rui Zhang
pmc-12679240.description: BACKGROUNDStem cell therapy has been recognized as a promising strategy for enhancing cardiac function after myocardial infarction. Nonetheless, its clinical benefits are frequently limited by the poor survival and differentiation rates of the transplanted cells.AIMTo clarify the role of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α)/β-catenin in survival and angiogenesis of peripheral blood mesenchymal stem cells (PBMSCs).

pmc-13062827.title: Contralateral axillary lymph node and chest wall skin recurrence 2 years after radical mastectomy for breast cancer: a case report and literature review
pmc-13062827.creator: Zhi-Yong Liu, Ran Chen
pmc-13062827.description: BackgroundContralateral axillary lymph node metastasis (CAM) following radical mastectomy for breast cancer is a rare and clinically challenging event, with a reported incidence of approximately 1.9% to 6.0%. Its pathogenesis, often attributed to altered lymphatic drainage after primary breast surgery, is not fully elucidated.

pmc-13187890.title: Current role of Histolog® in real-time histopathologic assessment: a systematic review
pmc-13187890.creator: Carlotta Liberale, Viscardo Paolo Fabbri, Sofia Passaseo, Daniele Marchioni, Stefania Corrado, Albino Eccher, Francesco Mattioli
pmc-13187890.description: SummaryAchieving complete tumor removal with negative margins remains a major goal in oncologic surgery. Frozen section analysis is still the most widely used method for intraoperative margin assessment, but it has several limitations, including time consumption, costs, and the need for dedicated pathology support.

uslaw-usc-t11-s1185.title: 11 U.S.C. § 1185 — Removal of debtor in possession
uslaw-usc-t11-s1185.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t11-s1185.description: United States Code, Title 11 (Bankruptcy); Chapter 11 (Reorganization); Subchapter V (Small Business Debtor Reorganization). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— On request of a party in interest, and after notice and a hearing, the court shall order that the debtor shall not be a debtor in possession for cause, including fraud, dishonesty, incompetence, or gross mismanagement of the affairs.
